title: Deterministic Boundaries: Why the AI Mock Is Predictable on Purpose — Check

questions.prompt: Why is a deterministic mock essential for writing meaningful tests around the AI search?
questions.explanation: A test is only an assertion if its expected value is stable. A non-deterministic LLM gives no fixed value to assert against; a deterministic mock does.
options: Because mocks are always faster than real services
Because a stable, fixed output lets you write exact assertions that only change when you change the code
Because Netlify cannot call real LLMs
Because deterministic mocks improve the model's accuracy

questions.prompt: Keeping the AI search as a separate, stubbed surface prevents the LLM's non-determinism from leaking into the gateway's core compute path.
questions.explanation: True. Isolating AI as an edge feature keeps the deterministic core verifiable and trustworthy, independent of model uncertainty.

questions.prompt: What does a deterministic AI mock NOT verify?
questions.explanation: The mock tests your system's handling of the model's contract. Judging the real model's output quality is a separate, probabilistic evaluation that belongs in its own suite.
options: That your code shapes the request correctly
That your code parses the response shape correctly
That the UI renders the results
